lore:
Separate. Experience. Swarm. Invade.
Scholars have long debated the true meaning of the Semitic root "p-l-sh" among the Philistines. For the first time in his life, Goliath felt that those ancient scholars had possessed genuine insight. These four brief words nearly encapsulated the entire life of a Philistine.

The Philistines were, indeed, a maritime people. They were like shoals of long-tailed sharks, drawn by the scent of blood toward islands where they could settle, only to slaughter the natives who lived there.
The Philistines never tired. They never lingered. Once everything had been taken, their restless instincts drove them onward in search of new prey.
They cared nothing for tomorrow. They squandered their plundered wealth with astonishing speed, drinking the last drop of wine, then breeding, fighting, and betraying one another with reckless abandon...

As they set sail, Goliath looked back at the trail their ships had left across the sea.
The blood of the Philistines. The blood of the natives. The blood of their enemies. The blood of seabirds...
It all merged together, like dark-red ink spilling into an endless blue.

The next day, the sun rose as usual. The sea shimmered like countless shards of broken gold, and everything vanished without a trace.
They were in the ocean, yet the ocean had forgotten them.
